So the modeled split is consistent with Google's own framework: the pack is gated by a factor the site can't control, and organic is won by factors it can.

**Measured corroboration (the harder backstop).** Sterling Sky analyzed 8,186 businesses across 200 cities with Places Scout — a quantitative study, not opinion. It found a negative correlation between hiding your address and pack rank, that this-month review *velocity* outranks total review count, and that landing pages with "more meaningful words" rank better ([Sterling Sky, "near me" 2025](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/what-gets-you-ranking-for-near-me-2025/)). Velocity is the fastest, most volatile lever: a client doing 60+ reviews/month dominated until going dormant 18 days, after which rankings "fell off a cliff" ([same study](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/what-gets-you-ranking-for-near-me-2025/)). This confirms the pack rewards a GBP/proximity/velocity bundle — none of which a one-time site build owns.

**Click-share — sized honestly, not hyped.** In 2025, ~44% of local clicks went to the pack, ~29% to organic, ~19% paid, ~8% to "more results" ([Monday Digital](https://mondaydigital.com/blog/google-local-pack-traffic-statistics/)). The pack wins the plurality head-to-head — so the case for organic is **scale and control**, not click-share. Pack CTRs are flat and proximity-gated (#1 ~17.8%, #2 ~15.4%, #3 ~15.1% — only ~3 points across top-3) ([same source](https://mondaydigital.com/blog/google-local-pack-traffic-statistics/)), so the pack is a near-default within one office radius (~5-7 miles), not a regional engine. Organic's ~29% scales across every town in the region and is the only surface a compounding deep-site budget can win.

**Durability — relative, not absolute.** As discovery shifts to AI, Whitespark's third 2026 column de-centers GBP further: on-page 24 / reviews 16 / citations 13 / links 13 / GBP 12 ([AdviceLocal](https://www.advicelocal.com/blog/2026-local-search-ranking-factors-maps-organic-ai/)). Sterling Sky measured AI local packs surfacing only ~32% as many businesses as traditional 3-packs across 322 markets (88% of markets showed fewer) ([Sterling Sky, State of Local SEO 2026](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/the-state-of-local-seo-in-2026/)) — the pack is compressing to 1-2 names. But organic is not immune: a randomized field experiment measured AI Overviews cutting organic clicks 38% on triggered queries ([SEJ on Agarwal & Sen, ISB/CMU 2026](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/ai-overviews-cut-organic-clicks-38-field-study-finds/573145/)). Honest frame: organic is the *more durable* of the two and the only one a deep site can win — not a forever-safe channel.

**What NOT to oversell:** the model is expert opinion, not Google's weights — sell the direction, not the decimals. The pack still wins ~44% of clicks (not 60-90%); organic's edge is scale and control, not raw click-share. And AI Overviews are eroding organic too — pitch relative durability, never immunity.

loadBearing.claim: In local ORGANIC rankings, on-page content (~33%) plus links (~24%) account for ~57% of modeled ranking weight — the majority of organic rank is won by the two levers a deep site plus one-time shippable off-page directly controls; GBP is only ~7% of organic.
loadBearing.stat: Organic: on-page 33% + links 24% = 57%; GBP 7%
loadBearing.snippet: For traditional website rankings below the map pack, your on-page optimization and backlink profile dominate, accounting for over 50% of the impact.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the engine of the entire organic-dominance offer — it is the headline number on the reel/slide and the justification for centering a deep site over the pack. If wrong, the offer's central claim collapses.

loadBearing.claim: The local PACK is dominated by GBP (~32%) plus reviews (~20%) = ~52%, both proximity-/profile-gated factors; on-page is only ~15% and links ~8% of the pack. The pack rewards the GBP/proximity bundle, not site depth.
loadBearing.stat: Pack: GBP 32% + reviews 20% = 52%; on-page 15%, links 8%
loadBearing.snippet: Combined, your Google Business Profile and reviews account for over half the ranking impact for map pack results.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the contrast half of the thesis — it justifies why we do NOT center the pack (a site can't move its dominant levers). Anchors the 'pack is a byproduct' framing in every pitch.

loadBearing.claim: The pack/organic split is a Whitespark expert-opinion survey (~47 local-search experts scoring 187 factors, aggregated by Darren Shaw), NOT Google-published weights — the percentages are directional ranks (±several points), not measured Google data.
loadBearing.stat: 47 experts, 187 factors, modeled (not Google-published)
loadBearing.snippet: Whitespark sends a comprehensive two-hour survey to 47 of the industry's leading local search experts ... 187 ranking factors ... Darren Shaw, founder of Whitespark
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: FTC-exposure guardrail. Every time T4-1 and T4-2 appear in reel/pitch copy, this disclosure must ride alongside or the numbers read as fabricated Google weights — the cardinal sin of false precision.

loadBearing.claim: MEASURED corroboration (not survey opinion): Sterling Sky analyzed 8,186 businesses across 200 cities with Places Scout and found a negative correlation between hiding your address and pack rank, that this-month review velocity outranks total review count, and that landing-page content substance correlates with rank.
loadBearing.stat: 8,186 businesses / 200 cities; measured study
loadBearing.snippet: We Analyzed 8,186 Businesses in 200 Cities ... negative correlation between hiding your address and ranking well in the local pack ... The number of reviews you've gotten this month matters more than your total number of reviews.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The hard, measured backstop under the modeled split — it's what answers a skeptic who dismisses the percentages as crowd-sourced opinion. Load-bearing for defensibility specifically because it is data-driven, not a survey.

loadBearing.claim: Click-share reality check: in 2025 ~44% of local clicks went to the pack vs ~29% organic, ~19% paid, ~8% more-results — the pack captures the plurality but NOT 60-90%, and the case for organic is scale and control, not click-share.
loadBearing.stat: Pack 44% / organic 29% / paid 19% / more-results 8% (2025)
loadBearing.snippet: 44% of local searchers clicked on Local Pack or Map Pack results, while 29% for organic results, 19% for paid results, and 8% for more local results.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Prevents overselling the pack's click dominance AND keeps the organic pitch honest — it forces the offer to argue scale/control rather than raw clicks. Goes on the slide that pre-empts the 'why not center the pack' objection.

whatNotToOversell: The pack/organic percentages are a Whitespark expert-opinion survey (47 experts, 187 factors), NOT Google-published weights — sell the direction (which levers dominate which surface), never the decimals as certified fact. No error bars are published; treat as ±several points.

Do NOT claim the pack is 60-90% of local clicks — it is ~44% in 2025 (organic ~29%). The pack actually wins the plurality head-to-head; organic's advantage is SCALE (region-wide vs ~5-7mi proximity cap) and CONTROL (the only surface a deep-site budget can compound), not click-share.

Do NOT pitch organic as a forever-safe channel. A randomized field study measured AI Overviews cutting organic clicks 38% on triggered queries — organic is the MORE durable of the two surfaces and the only one a deep site can win, not immune to AI erosion.

Do NOT sell the pack as a site-driven win. Proximity is a hard geographic cap a website cannot overcome; 'on-page 15% of pack' overstates how much a deep site moves the pack for a far-away searcher. The pack is a proximity-capped byproduct we deliver, never center.

The primary whitespark.ca report is JS-rendered and rests on agency summaries here. Two independent detailed summaries plus BrightLocal and a separate Moz model corroborate the direction, but a verifier should confirm against the rendered Whitespark report before FTC-exposed reel copy ships.

Exclude all PBN / link-scheme / gray-hat tactics explicitly. The link weight in the organic split is earned via legitimate one-time shippable off-page only; ongoing client-managed off-page is out of scope for this pillar.
gaps: Primary whitespark.ca/local-search-ranking-factors/ page is JavaScript-rendered and was not directly machine-readable in this pass; the full-column figures rest on three independent agency summaries of it. A verifier should confirm the rendered report (or PDF) to lock the exact 2026 percentages before FTC-exposed reel copy.
No published error bars / variance for the Whitespark survey weights — they are point estimates from 47 experts. Cannot state a defensible +/- range numerically; can only label 'directional'.

Roofing-specific pack-vs-organic click split not isolated; the 44/29 figure is general local-search. A roofing-specific behavioral source (longer sales cycle favoring organic touchpoints) would strengthen the vertical fit.
Sterling Sky's measured study covered plumber/HVAC/locksmith/garage-door/lawn-care, not roofing specifically — proximity/velocity findings are highly transferable but not roofing-measured.

Did not pull a BrightLocal independent corroborator this pass (Firecrawl out of credits limited search breadth); a BrightLocal consumer/ranking study would add a second independent (non-Whitespark) anchor on the pack-importance side.

No roofing-/home-services-vertical or NC/Triangle-specific pack-vs-organic split exists in any source found — all weighting models are cross-vertical. The vertical framing must stay directional ('for high-ticket roofing') and cannot cite a roofing-specific weighting number.

No Google FIRST-PARTY published weight exists for any factor (Google only confirms the relevance/distance/prominence pillars, never percentages). The 32/20/15 pack and 33/24 organic figures are forever modeled — there is no primary measured weighting to upgrade them to.

The Searchlab page attributes a Moz 'GBP 36% / on-page 16% / links 13%' pack model and a separate '42% pack click share (Moz 2026)' — these were captured via the aggregator page, not Moz's own LSRF page; a direct Moz primary-source confirmation of the 2026 model was not obtained (firecrawl out of credits, Moz page not fetched).

AI-local-pack click-share / conversion data is early (Sterling Sky reports business-coverage shrinkage and call-button removal, not a clean post-AI organic-vs-pack CLICK split) — the 44% pack / 29% organic click split from round 1 predates the AI-pack rollout and may be shifting.

counter.point: The entire pack/organic split is an EXPERT-OPINION SURVEY (47 people scoring factors), not measured Google data. A skeptic can dismiss any single percentage as crowd-sourced opinion with no error bars published. Treat numbers as directional ranks (+/- several points), never as precise weights — promise the pattern (on-page+links dominate organic), not the decimal.
counter.soWhat: Frame in pitches as 'industry's largest expert consensus' and the DIRECTION (which levers dominate which surface), never as a Google-certified weight. The Sterling Sky measured study is the harder backstop for the proximity/velocity/content claims.

counter.point: Secondhand summaries disagree at the margins: one search-engine summary reported pack as on-page 19 / reviews 16 / links 15 (closer to older/2023 editions or a category mislabel), versus the 15/20/8 confirmed by two detailed sources. The primary whitespark.ca page is JS-rendered and was not directly machine-readable here — the figures rest on agency summaries of it.
counter.soWhat: Two independent detailed summaries (AdviceLocal, Kyle Eggleston) agree exactly on the full pack column and one (Sam Bretzmann) on the organic top-3, so confidence is high — but a verifier should ideally confirm against the rendered whitespark.ca report before it goes into FTC-exposed reel copy.

counter.point: Proximity is the confound the survey-category buckets hide: in the PACK, GBP-category + proximity + address are top individual factors, and proximity is a hard geographic cap no amount of on-page/links overcomes within a competitor's tighter radius. So 'on-page 15% of pack' overstates how much a site can move the pack for a far-away searcher.
counter.soWhat: Reinforces the spine: do NOT sell the pack as a site-driven win — sell ORGANIC regional dominance (where on-page+links = 57%) and treat the pack as the proximity-capped ~5-7mi byproduct. Never naively sum proximity into a category bucket.

counter.point: Click-share (pack 44% vs organic 29%) means the PACK still wins the most local clicks head-to-head. A skeptic says 'so why not center the pack?' The answer is scale + control: the pack is proximity-capped to one office radius and flat across positions, while organic scales region-wide and is the only surface a $5-10k/mo deep-site + off-page budget can compound.
counter.soWhat: Position organic as the regional-scale ENGINE and the pack as the local near-default it also captures — rank the prizes, sell the bigger. Do not claim pack is '60-90%' of clicks; it is ~44%.

counter.point: Organic is NOT immune to the AI-search erosion that is hitting the pack. A randomized field experiment (Agarwal & Sen, Indian School of Business / Carnegie Mellon, SSRN April 2026; 1,065 US participants, Jan-Feb 2026) MEASURED that AI Overviews cut organic clicks on triggered queries by 38%.
counter.soWhat: Do not pitch organic as a forever-safe channel just because the pack is shrinking. The honest frame: organic is the MORE durable of the two and the only one a deep site can actually win, but AI Overviews are compressing organic clicks too — so the offer is about relative durability + capturing the AI-overview citation (which content+links+citations earn, per round 1's AI-visibility column), not immunity.

counter.point: Reviews/GBP alone will not make a site rank organically, and conversely a weak site can still hold the map pack on proximity + reviews alone (the 'mechanic with good reviews and close proximity ranks in the map despite poor website optimization' case).
counter.soWhat: Cuts both ways but mostly supports the pillar: it confirms a deep site is REQUIRED for organic (the prize we sell) and that the pack is a proximity-gated near-default we can't fully engineer with site depth. Keep the spine — sell organic dominance, deliver the pack as the proximity-capped byproduct; never imply the site alone guarantees the pack.

counter.point: The headline pack-vs-organic percentage split is a MODELED expert-opinion survey (Whitespark: ~47 experts scoring 187 factors; Moz: a separate expert model), not Google-published or measured weights — and the two models disagree at the margin (Whitespark pack GBP 32% vs Moz pack GBP ~36%).
counter.soWhat: Always label the percentages as 'modeled expert consensus, directional +/- points,' cite TWO independent models (Whitespark + Moz agree on ordering), and lean on the MEASURED studies (Sterling Sky proximity/velocity/content; the 38% RCT) for the load-bearing claims. The ordering is robust across models even though exact points are not. Promise the FLOOR (organic majority is won by on-page+links the site controls), project the CEILING.

allClaims.claim: Whitespark's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors gives the LOCAL PACK (Maps) thematic category split as: GBP signals 32%, review signals 20%, on-page signals 15%, behavioral signals 9%, link signals 8%, citation signals 6%, personalization 6%. This confirms the seed pack column.
allClaims.stat: Pack: GBP 32 / reviews 20 / on-page 15 / behavioral 9 / links 8 / citations 6 / personalization 6
allClaims.snippet: Local Pack/Maps: GBP Signals: 32%, Review Signals: 20%, On-Page Signals: 15%, Link Signals: 8%, Behavioral Signals: 9%, Citation Signals: 6%, Personalization: 6%

allClaims.claim: Whitespark's 2026 LSRF gives the LOCAL ORGANIC split as: on-page signals 33%, link signals 24%, behavioral 10%, personalization 8%, GBP 7%, citations 7%, reviews 6%. This confirms the seed organic column (on-page 33 / links 24 / GBP 7).
allClaims.stat: Organic: on-page 33 / links 24 / behavioral 10 / personalization 8 / GBP 7 / citations 7 / reviews 6
allClaims.snippet: Local Organic: On-Page Signals: 33%, Link Signals: 24%, Behavioral Signals: 10%, Personalization: 8%, GBP Signals: 7%, Citation Signals: 7%, Review Signals: 6%

allClaims.claim: THE LOAD-BEARING TAKEAWAY: in Local Organic, on-page (33%) + links (24%) = ~57% of modeled ranking weight — the majority of organic rank is won by the two levers a deep site plus one-time shippable off-page directly controls. GBP is only ~7% of organic. This is the engine of the organic-dominance offer.
allClaims.stat: on-page 33 + links 24 = 57% of organic; GBP only 7% of organic
allClaims.snippet: For traditional website rankings below the map pack, your on-page optimization and backlink profile dominate, accounting for over 50% of the impact.

allClaims.claim: Conversely, the LOCAL PACK is dominated by GBP (32%) + reviews (20%) = ~52% — both proximity-/profile-gated factors. On-page is only 15% and links only 8% of the pack. The pack rewards the GBP/proximity bundle, not site depth.
allClaims.stat: GBP 32 + reviews 20 = 52% of pack; on-page 15, links 8
allClaims.snippet: Combined, your Google Business Profile and reviews account for over half the ranking impact for map pack results.

allClaims.claim: The split is a MODELED expert-opinion survey, NOT Google-published weights: Whitespark's 2026 report aggregates a ~two-hour survey of 47 leading local-search experts scoring 187 factors. The percentages are aggregated expert opinion (directional, +/- points), not measured Google data — flag this every time the numbers are cited.
allClaims.stat: 47 experts surveyed, 187 factors, by Darren Shaw (Whitespark founder)
allClaims.snippet: Whitespark sends a comprehensive two-hour survey to 47 of the industry's leading local search experts ... 187 ranking factors ... Darren Shaw, founder of Whitespark

allClaims.claim: Independent second source confirms the identical pack split (GBP 32 / reviews 20 / on-page 15 / behavioral 9 / links 8 / citations 6 / personalization 6), reducing single-source risk on the pack column.
allClaims.stat: Pack column identical to AdviceLocal across an independent summary
allClaims.snippet: GBP signals: 32% ... Review signals: 20% ... On-page signals: 15% ... Behavioral signals: 9% ... Link signals: 8% ... Citation signals: 6% ... Personalization: 6%

allClaims.claim: MEASURED corroboration that proximity/address and review velocity are real pack levers (not just survey opinion): Sterling Sky analyzed 8,186 businesses across 200 cities (with Places Scout) — a quantitative measured study, not opinion. It found a negative correlation between hiding your address and pack ranking, and that this-month review velocity outranks total review count.
allClaims.stat: 8,186 businesses / 200 cities; measured (top-10 pack per term, tens of thousands of data points)
allClaims.snippet: We Analyzed 8,186 Businesses in 200 Cities ... negative correlation between hiding your address and ranking well in the local pack ... The number of reviews you've gotten this month matters more than your total number of reviews.

allClaims.claim: Sterling Sky's measured study found review VELOCITY is the fastest, most volatile pack lever: a dental client with 60+ reviews/month dominated until going dormant 18 days, after which rankings 'fell off a cliff.' This is measured behavior corroborating the modeled ~20% pack review weight.
allClaims.stat: 60+ reviews/month dominated; rankings collapsed after 18 days dormant
allClaims.snippet: A dental client with 60+ monthly reviews dominated the rankings until stopping for 18 days, after which rankings fell off a cliff.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: measured (client case data within the study)

allClaims.claim: Sterling Sky measured that landing-page content substance correlates with pack rank — 'more meaningful words' on the landing page (not raw volume), independently corroborating that on-page still matters (the modeled ~15% pack / ~33% organic on-page weight) and that a deep site helps even on the proximity-capped pack.
allClaims.stat: content substance (meaningful words) positively correlated with rank
allClaims.snippet: More meaningful words on landing pages correlate with better rankings, not simply volume.

allClaims.claim: Click-share reality check (do NOT oversell the pack): in 2025 ~44% of local-search clicks went to the Local Pack vs ~29% to organic, ~19% paid, ~8% 'more local results.' The pack captures the plurality but NOT 60-90% — and organic's ~29% is the regional-dominance prize the deep site wins.
allClaims.stat: Pack 44% / organic 29% / paid 19% / more-results 8% of local clicks (2025)
allClaims.snippet: 44% of local searchers clicked on Local Pack or Map Pack results, while 29% for organic results, 19% for paid results, and 8% for more local results.

allClaims.claim: Per-position pack CTRs are flat and proximity-gated: #1 pack ~17.8%, #2 ~15.4%, #3 ~15.1% — only ~3 points separate top-3, and proximity caps which businesses even appear. This is why the pack is a near-default byproduct within ~5-7 miles, not a scalable regional engine.
allClaims.snippet: The #1 local pack result received 17.8% of click-throughs, followed by 15.4% for #2 and 15.1% for #3.

allClaims.claim: Whitespark's third 2026 column (AI search visibility) further de-centers GBP: on-page 24%, reviews 16%, citations 13%, links 13%, GBP 12%, personalization 9%, behavioral 4%. As local discovery shifts to AI overviews, the content+links+citations bundle (a deep site delivers) outweighs GBP — reinforcing the organic-first thesis for durability.
allClaims.stat: AI search: on-page 24 / reviews 16 / citations 13 / links 13 / GBP 12 / personalization 9 / behavioral 4
allClaims.snippet: AI Search Visibility Factors: On-Page Signals: 24%, Review Signals: 16%, Citation Signals: 13%, Link Signals: 13%, GBP Signals: 12%, Personalization: 9%, Behavioral Signals: 4%

allClaims.claim: Google's own local algorithm is built on three pillars — relevance, distance (proximity), and prominence — and proximity/distance is the pillar unique to the map pack that a website cannot control. This is the primary-framework anchor under the modeled Whitespark split: the pack column is dominated by GBP+proximity factors a deep site does not influence, while the organic column is won by on-page/links/prominence the site does control.
allClaims.snippet: Proximity: 'The physical distance between the user's search query and the business' ... Prominence: Reflects how well-known and trusted a business is, influenced by backlinks, social mentions, reviews, and web references. Local Pack (Maps) prioritizes: Google Business Profile (32% importance), Reviews (20%), On-page factors (15%). Local Organic prioritizes: On-page optimization (33%), Links (24%), Behavioral signals (10%).
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: Google's three-pillar framework is first-party/directional; the percentage split is modeled (Whitespark expert survey, here reproduced independently by BrightLocal).
allClaims.source_type_note: BrightLocal independently reproduces the same pack-vs-organic split round 1 sourced from Whitespark — a second independent corroborator of the load-bearing split.
allClaims.stat: Pack: GBP 32 / reviews 20 / on-page 15. Organic: on-page 33 / links 24 / behavioral 10.

allClaims.claim: An independent third source (Searchlab 2026 local-SEO statistics) cross-confirms via Moz's Local Search Ranking Factors that the local PACK is GBP-dominated (GBP ~36%, on-page ~16%, links ~13%) and that proximity is the single strongest individual pack factor — corroborating, from a different model (Moz, not Whitespark), that the pack rewards the GBP/proximity bundle and not site depth.
allClaims.snippet: GBP Signals (proximity, categories, keyword in name) 36% | On-Page Signals (NAP, domain authority, keywords) 16% | Link Signals 13% — Source: Moz Local Search Ranking Factors 2026. '#1 Proximity is the strongest individual ranking factor' — Whitespark Local Ranking Study 2026.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: modeled (Moz LSRF expert model) — reduces single-model risk by corroborating the Whitespark split with an independent model giving the same directional ordering.
allClaims.stat: Moz pack model: GBP 36 / on-page 16 / links 13.

allClaims.claim: MEASURED, primary corroboration that the pack and organic results are driven by DIFFERENT mechanisms: Sterling Sky's State of Local SEO 2026 analyzed 322 markets and found AI local packs surfaced only 5,943 unique businesses vs 18,330 in traditional 3-packs — about 32% as many, an ~68% reduction, with 88% of markets showing fewer businesses in the AI pack. As Google compresses the pack to 1-2 businesses and strips call buttons, the durable visibility channel shifts to organic/content the deep site controls — directly reinforcing the organic-first thesis.
allClaims.snippet: AI local packs featured 5,943 unique businesses whereas, regular 3-packs featured 18,330. ... AI local packs are only surfacing about 32% as many businesses as traditional 3-packs. ... In the 322 markets we looked at, 88% had fewer unique businesses in the AI local packs than traditional local packs.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: measured (Joy Hawkins / Sterling Sky, Places Scout ranking data across 322 markets) — quantitative, not opinion survey.
allClaims.stat: 5,943 vs 18,330 unique businesses; ~32% / -68%; 88% of 322 markets.

allClaims.claim: Independent practitioner sources (Search Engine Land case study; BoostMyBusiness) confirm the mechanism is genuinely bifurcated: a business can rank organically while losing the pack, and vice versa, because organic rank is driven by content quality, internal linking, keyword relevance, backlinks and technical SEO, while the pack is driven by location/proximity, reviews, categories and GBP activity. This is the qualitative 'why' behind the modeled split — the levers a deep site plus one-time shippable off-page controls are precisely the organic levers.
allClaims.snippet: When Google ranks websites organically, it looks at things like: Content quality, Page speed, Internal linking, Keyword relevance, Backlinks, Website structure, User experience, Technical SEO. [GBP map pack is] heavily influenced by local signals... Business location, Reviews, Business categories, GBP activity, Photos, Consistency across the web, Distance from the searcher.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: directional/qualitative practitioner explanation — supporting color, not a primary weighting source.

pillars.title: Tier-1 manual citations
pillars.section:
## L2 — Tier-1 Manual Citations: build the foundation once, then stop

**Bottom line:** Citations are table-stakes, not a dominance lever. You build a clean, consistent set of high-trust listings one time, then you are done. They remove a trust/NAP deficit so the deep site and reviews can do the organic lifting — they do not move organic rank on their own. King Maker ships this as a one-time foundation pass, never as a monthly KPI.

**One-time, not ongoing.** Whitespark founder Darren Shaw's position is explicit: build the top 30-50 directories and "once you've done that you are done," and the era of chasing 500 citations "is over" ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/blog/do-citations-matter-local-seo/)). He also rejects recurring listing fees for any business under ~100 locations ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/blog/do-citations-matter-local-seo/)). This is the spine of the one-time-shippable scope: 30-50 consistent citations is plenty for most local businesses, beyond which returns diminish fast, and cleaning inaccurate/duplicate listings beats building new ones on a broken foundation ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/blog/do-citations-matter-local-seo/)).

**Citation vs. link equity — read this honestly.** Most of the tier-1 set is nofollow: BBB, Houzz, Nextdoor, Angi, Thumbtack, and Yellow Pages all carry nofollow links per BrightLocal's primary table ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)). The seed premise that "most citations are nofollow" is directionally correct for that lead-gen/review tier. But it is wrong for the four highest-value infrastructure listings: Apple Business Connect (DA99), Yelp (DA93), Bing Maps (DA93), and HomeAdvisor (DA78) are dofollow per the same table ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)). Honest framing: the most valuable citations to build are dofollow AND free AND highest-trust, not nofollow afterthoughts. Two cautions on the equity claim — (1) DA is a Moz third-party metric, not a Google ranking factor, and a high site DA does not mean high passed equity from a deep, templated profile page ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)); (2) dofollow/nofollow is page-level and shifts over time, so spot-verify the live profile's rel attribute before any equity claim. Default to "treat as nofollow trust signal unless verified." Nofollow listings from authoritative domains still send trust/discovery signals and referral traffic — value them for NAP consistency and entity trust, never as "backlinks" ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)).

**The ranked build order (NC roofer, impact-vs-effort):**
- **Tier A — free + dofollow/highest-trust (build first):** Apple Business Connect (DA99 dofollow, free, and an AI-verification node feeding Siri/Spotlight/Apple Intelligence — [pinmeto.com](https://www.pinmeto.com/blog/apple-business-connect-listings-2026/)), Yelp (DA93 dofollow), Bing Places/Maps (DA93 dofollow, free, feeds Copilot — [brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/local-listings-management-explained/)), and the NCLBGC state-license profile — a quasi-.gov entity-trust citation searchable at [portal.nclbgc.org](http://portal.nclbgc.org/Public/Search) (an S-Roofing specialty license is required for any roofing project $40,000+).
- **Tier B — free + nofollow, entity trust:** BBB (DA91), Houzz (DA86, roofing-relevant), Nextdoor (DA83, hyperlocal), Yellow Pages (DA62) ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)). Add the free high-DA contractor verticals — BuildZoom (DA60), Procore (DA59), The Blue Book (DA53), GuildQuality (DA50) ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/industry/contractors/)).
- **Tier C — paid/lead-gen, claim for entity validation only, flag honestly:** Angi (DA76 nofollow), HomeAdvisor (DA78 dofollow but FTC-flagged), Thumbtack (DA76 nofollow), local Chamber (~$200-500/yr, link often nofollow on third-party platforms — [echamber.com](https://echamber.com/blog/SEO-benefits-of-chamber-membership/)). The FTC ordered HomeAdvisor (Angi-owned) to pay up to $7.2M over deceptively marketed leads ([ftc.gov](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2023/01/ftc-order-requires-homeadvisor-pay-72-million-stop-deceptively-marketing-its-leads-home-improvement)). Never recommend paying for Angi/HomeAdvisor leads as part of the citation strategy — claim the listing for NAP validation, full stop.

**Approximate one-time cost:** Tiers A and B are free (labor only — a one-time manual submission/claim pass across ~20-30 listings). Tier C, if pursued at all, is the only paid line: a local Chamber runs roughly **$200-500/yr** ($125 floor), and that is the only recurring fee in the stack — Whitespark's guidance is to skip recurring listing fees entirely under 100 locations ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/blog/do-citations-matter-local-seo/)).

**Impact-vs-effort read:** LOW-to-MODERATE impact, LOW one-time effort, HIGH insurance value. The floor: a clean consistent NAP foundation removes a trust deficit and a duplicate-listing penalty. The ceiling: improved entity trust plus emerging AI-visibility (Apple/Bing feeding Siri, Spotlight, Copilot) — directional, not measured. This is foundation/insurance, not differentiation. The deep site, reviews, and earned topically-relevant links are the organic-dominance levers; citations just keep you from starting in a hole.

**What NOT to oversell:** Do not sell citations as a rank booster — independent consensus is they are foundational, not a needle-mover ([jemsu.com](https://jemsu.com/do-local-citations-still-matter-for-seo-in-2024/)). Do not use the unsourced "NAP consistency = 40% more likely to appear in the pack" stat — it fails the primary-source bar. Do not let high DA numbers imply high passed link equity. Promise the floor (a clean foundation), project the ceiling (entity + AI trust), and never headline citations as the engine.

loadBearing.claim: Citation building is a one-time foundation, not an ongoing program: build the top 30-50 directories and you are done; chasing 500 citations is over; no recurring listing fees under ~100 locations.
loadBearing.stat: Top 30-50 directories then done; 500-citation era 'over'; no recurring fees under 100 locations
loadBearing.snippet: 'Once you've done that you are done.' ... 'I don't think you should go and build up 500 citations on every directory you can find' and 'I think that those days are done, that concept of citation building is over.' ... 'I also don't think you need to pay recurring fees for listings, unless you are a multi-location operation with 100 plus locations.'
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the spine of the one-time-shippable-off-page scope and the offer's honesty boundary — it justifies why KM ships citations once and refuses to bill them monthly. Sourced to Whitespark's founder (the primary independent authority on citations), it directly anchors the 'build once, stop' thesis.

loadBearing.claim: The tier-1 dofollow/nofollow split: Apple Business Connect (DA99), Yelp (DA93), Bing Maps (DA93), and HomeAdvisor (DA78) are dofollow; BBB (DA91), Houzz (DA86), Nextdoor (DA83), Angi (DA76), Thumbtack (DA76), and Yellow Pages (DA62) are nofollow.
loadBearing.stat: 4 dofollow (ABC/Yelp/Bing/HomeAdvisor); 6 nofollow (BBB/Angi/Houzz/Nextdoor/Thumbtack/YP)
loadBearing.snippet: Apple Business Connect 99 DoFollow; Yelp 93 DoFollow; Bing Maps 93 DoFollow; HomeAdvisor 78 DoFollow appear in the DoFollow column, while BBB, Angi, Houzz, Nextdoor, Thumbtack and Yellow Pages appear in the NoFollow column.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Goes directly onto the build-order slide and corrects the seed's 'most citations are nofollow' framing — the equity vs. citation distinction the whole pillar pivots on. Misstating which listings are dofollow is the FTC-exposed false-confidence trap, so it must be cited and spot-verifiable.

loadBearing.claim: The FTC ordered HomeAdvisor (Angi-owned) to pay up to $7.2M and stop deceptively marketing leads to home-improvement contractors; leads often did not match promised services/geography.
loadBearing.stat: FTC: up to $7.2M; leads sold to multiple contractors
loadBearing.snippet: FTC Order Requires HomeAdvisor to Pay Up To $7.2 Million and Stop Deceptively Marketing its Leads for Home Improvement Projects... while HomeAdvisor represented that service providers only would receive leads matching the types of services they provide and their preferred geographic area, many of them do not.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the load-bearing reason KM never recommends paying for Angi/HomeAdvisor leads — it protects the offer from a customer-hostile recommendation and is a .gov primary source. It governs the Tier-C 'entity-validation-only, flag honestly' rule that keeps the pitch defensible.

loadBearing.claim: Citations are foundational, not a ranking booster: independent consensus is the role of citations as a ranking signal declines yearly — hard to rank without them, but other tactics move the needle more.
loadBearing.stat: Citations = foundational factor, not rankings booster
loadBearing.snippet: citations are more of a foundational factor than a rankings booster — you'll have a hard time ranking without them, but other tactics will be more likely to move the needle.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the cardinal honesty guardrail for the pillar: it forbids selling citations as an organic-rank lever. It directly enforces the spine (citations are a proximity-/trust-floor, the deep site does the lifting) and keeps the reel/pitch FTC-safe.

loadBearing.claim: Apple Business Connect is free, dofollow (DA99), and an AI-verification node feeding Siri/Spotlight/Apple Intelligence — making it the single highest-value free citation on both link and AEO grounds; Bing Places is the free Microsoft equivalent feeding Copilot.
loadBearing.stat: ABC free + DA99 dofollow + AI node; Bing free + DA93 dofollow + feeds Copilot
loadBearing.snippet: Apple Business Connect is one of a small number of trusted nodes that AI systems verify your business against, with investment here improving local AI visibility everywhere, not just on iOS.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Anchors the 'Tier A, build first' priority and the forward-looking AEO angle that differentiates the foundation pass. Flagged vendor-incentive (PinMeTo) — the dofollow/DA99 leg is independently corroborated by BrightLocal, but the AI-node claim is directional and must be labeled as such, not promised.

whatNotToOversell: Do not sell citations as an organic-rank booster — independent 2024 consensus is they are foundational/table-stakes, not a needle-mover (jemsu.com). They prevent a deficit; they do not drive dominance.
Do not use the unsourced 'NAP consistency = 40% more likely to appear in the local pack' stat — it has no primary-study corroboration and fails the citation bar.

Do not let high Domain Authority numbers (DA99 Apple, DA93 Yelp) imply high passed link equity — DA is a Moz third-party metric, not a Google factor, and deep templated profile pages pass little equity.
Do not assert dofollow from a table — rel status is page-level and changes; default to 'nofollow trust signal unless the live profile is spot-verified.'
Do not recommend paying for Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack leads as part of the citation strategy — FTC-flagged, shared-lead marketplaces; claim the listing for NAP/entity validation only.
Do not headline citations as the organic-dominance engine — they are a one-time foundation; the deep site, reviews, and earned topically-relevant links are the actual levers.
Do not present the Apple/Bing AI-visibility benefit as measured — it is directional/AEO-emerging and partly vendor-sourced; project it as a ceiling, not a promise.
Do not frame Tier C Chamber/lead-gen fees as required — the only defensible cost line is the optional ~$200-500/yr Chamber; Whitespark says skip recurring listing fees under 100 locations.
gaps: Exact per-platform live rel-attribute (dofollow vs nofollow/ugc) was not spot-verified on each live profile template this session — BrightLocal's aggregated table is the source; verify live before any link-equity claim in a pitch.

No primary Apple/Microsoft first-party documentation captured confirming the AI-verification/AEO role of ABC/Bing — current support is vendor (PinMeTo) and an independent listings-management explainer; flagged vendor-incentive. A Google/Apple/Microsoft first-party doc would harden it.
DA figures are Moz-proprietary and undated in the fetched table; they are directional authority proxies, not Google signals, and may have drifted.

NC-specific local chamber link attributes (e.g., Charlotte/Raleigh chambers) were not individually verified — only the general nofollow-third-party pattern; per-client the specific chamber's directory link should be checked.
Yelp's well-documented anti-solicitation review policy (do not ask for Yelp reviews) intersects with the FTC fake-review rule and should be handled in the reviews pillar, not assumed here.
Houzz/Nextdoor roofing-specific citation value vs generic was inferred from home-services guidance, not a roofing-specific study.

Exact verbatim rank numbers from the Whitespark 2026 report ('best of' #1, industry-domains #3, unstructured #4) come from search-engine synthesis of the report, not a direct scrape of the report body (JS-rendered; WebFetch returned only chrome). Confidence is medium pending a direct read of whitespark.ca/local-search-ranking-factors or the published PDF/LinkedIn post by Darren Shaw.

No primary source found quantifying the dofollow/nofollow attribute of the contractor-vertical directories specifically (BuildZoom, Procore, GuildQuality, The Blue Book) — round 1's dofollow/nofollow table covers the general tier only. Each would need individual link-attribute verification before being priced as link equity.

No NC/Triangle-specific citation-impact data (e.g., a Raleigh/Charlotte geo-grid study) was found — the NC angle remains the state license + chamber, not a measured local-pack citation lift for the region.

Foursquare itself was not yet validated as a buildable one-time citation node (free listing claim flow, DA, dofollow status) despite driving 60-70% of small-town ChatGPT results — worth a dedicated lookup before adding it to the tier-1 build order.

Firecrawl search/scrape returned 402 (out of credits) for the entire session; all findings came via WebSearch + WebFetch fallback. A re-run with Firecrawl could surface the full Whitespark report body and BrightLocal tables more completely.

counter.point: Domain Authority (DA) is a Moz third-party proprietary metric, not a Google ranking factor — the DA numbers (DA99 Apple, DA93 Yelp) describe the domain's overall link profile, NOT the link equity actually passed to a roofer's site from a deep, often-templated, nofollow-by-default profile page. High site DA does not mean a high-value link to the client.
counter.soWhat: Do not let high-DA numbers in the pitch imply high passed link equity. Frame citations as entity/NAP/trust signals; reserve the link-equity claim for the genuinely dofollow + topically-relevant set (manufacturer find-a-pro, L3).

counter.point: Dofollow/nofollow status is page-level and changes over time; a directory listed as 'dofollow' in an aggregated table may render nofollow/UGC on the actual profile template, and many platforms moved listing links to nofollow/ugc. The BrightLocal column is a useful map but should be spot-verified per live profile before any link-equity claim.
counter.soWhat: Spot-check the live profile's rel attribute at build time rather than asserting dofollow from a table; the honest default is 'treat as nofollow trust signal unless verified.'

counter.point: Whitespark's expert consensus is that citation building 'is over' as a needle-mover — so even the highest-DA citations are foundation/insurance, not a dominance lever. Centering citations risks overselling table-stakes as differentiation.
counter.soWhat: Position the citation pass as a one-time foundation that prevents a deficit, then move budget to content + reviews + earned topically-relevant links (the actual organic-dominance levers). Do not headline citations.

counter.point: HomeAdvisor shows as dofollow DA78 in the table, which could tempt a 'build it for the link' pitch — but the FTC action and shared-lead/sales-pressure dynamics make it an actively customer-hostile platform to recommend; the link value does not offset the marketplace downside for the client.
counter.soWhat: Claim the listing for entity validation only if at all; never recommend paying for HomeAdvisor/Angi leads as part of the citation strategy. Flag the FTC history if the client asks.

counter.point: Skeptic consensus: citations are foundational, NOT a ranking BOOSTER. Multiple 2024 analyses converge that 'the role of citations as a ranking signal declines every year' and 'citations are more of a foundational factor than a rankings booster — you'll have a hard time ranking without them, but other tactics will be more likely to move the needle.'
counter.soWhat: KM must NOT sell citations as a lever that moves organic rank. Frame them honestly as table-stakes / a clean foundation that prevents a penalty/trust gap, while the deep SITE + reviews + GBP do the actual organic lifting. Overstating citations as a rank driver is the FTC-exposed false-confidence trap.

counter.point: The 'NAP consistency = 40% more likely to appear in the local pack' stat circulating in SEO blogs is unsourced/uncorroborated to a primary study and reads as a vendor talking point.
counter.soWhat: Do NOT use the '40% more likely' figure in any reel/pitch — it fails the no-retrofitted-citation / primary-source bar. Promise the floor (consistent NAP removes a trust deficit) and leave the percentage out.

counter.point: The contractor lead-gen directories that carry the highest DA on BrightLocal's contractor list (HomeAdvisor DA78, Porch DA76, Networx) are the same paid marketplaces round 1 flagged for FTC-sanctioned deceptive-lead practices and shared/sold leads.
counter.soWhat: Reinforces: claim these for entity/NAP validation ONLY, never as link assets or as a lead source we endorse. The high DA is real but the link is nofollow (Angi/Thumbtack) or the marketplace dynamics are adversarial — value is entity-trust, capped.

pillars.title: Manufacturer / credential backlinks
pillars.section:
## L3 — Manufacturer / Credential Backlinks

**Bottom line.** A roofer's manufacturer and trade-credential profiles are the single highest-relevance backlinks a contractor can earn — roofing-native, on a large trusted domain, and tied to a real gated credential ([footbridgemedia.com](https://www.footbridgemedia.com/marketing-tips/backlinks-for-home-service-pros)). The common gap is that certified roofers qualify for these listings but the website link is missing from their manufacturer profile — fixable with one rep call in under an hour ([footbridgemedia.com](https://www.footbridgemedia.com/marketing-tips/backlinks-for-home-service-pros)). That is the deliverable King Maker secures at launch.

**Why it matters for organic dominance.** Relevance beats raw Domain Authority — a topically-roofing link outranks a higher-DA off-topic link ([localroofingseo.agency](https://www.localroofingseo.agency/blog/link-building-for-roofing-contractors)). Manufacturer locators are roofing-native and credential-gated, which is exactly the relevance Google weighs most heavily. These links feed the organic-prominence engine; they do not move the proximity-capped map pack on their own.

**One-time, not ongoing.** This is a one-time shippable win: claim the listing, add the missing website link, deepen the profile with services/towns and link it to specific service pages rather than only the homepage ([roofingseo.services](https://roofingseo.services/link-building/how-to-get-backlinks-for-roofing-websites/)). It is not a recurring link-building retainer.

**Earn-not-buy, strictly gated.** The credential must already be held. The manufacturers state the bars are steep: GAF Master Elite ~top 2-3% of US contractors, requiring ~7 years experience and ≥$1M insurance ([thrushandson.com](https://www.thrushandson.com/home-improvement-blog/gaf-master-elite/)); Owens Corning Platinum Preferred <1%, invitation-only, ≥3 years same ownership ([roofon.com](https://roofon.com/owens-corning-platinum-preferred-contractor/)); CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster <1%, requiring all field supervisors and ≥50% of installers MSA-credentialed ([certainteed.com](https://www.certainteed.com/select-shinglemaster)). For an uncertified client, this pillar yields only the association and distributor tier — there is no PBN, purchase, or link-scheme substitute, explicitly excluded.

**Dofollow vs. citation — UNVERIFIED.** I could not confirm this session whether GAF / Owens Corning / CertainTeed locator listings emit a dofollow external link to the contractor's own domain, link only to an internal manufacturer profile, or are nofollow / JS-rendered ([gaf.com](https://www.gaf.com/en-us/roofing-contractors/residential)). GAF blocked automated fetch. Until a live per-manufacturer HTML check confirms (a) the contractor's external domain is present, (b) no rel=nofollow/ugc/sponsored, (c) server-rendered without JS, treat these as **relevance / trust / AI-citation signals**, not confirmed link equity. pillars.title: On-site local-proof layer (what WE build)
pillars.section:
## PILLAR L4 — On-site local-proof layer (what WE build)

**Bottom line:** The on-site local-proof layer is a one-time, shippable build — LocalBusiness/Organization schema with geo coordinates and `sameAs`, consistent shown NAP, embedded map and driving directions, an aggregateRating block, and genuinely unique per-city/service pages. Its biggest payoff is **organic regional dominance**, not the map pack. On-page is the single largest organic ranking lever — modeled at ~33% of organic weight by an expert survey ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/local-search-ranking-factors/)) — while it is a minority of pack weight (~15%). Google ranks local on relevance, distance, and prominence, and prominence explicitly counts "your position in web results," so SEO best practices apply ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091)). The website's job is to win organic and to *verify* the entity for the pack — it does not out-weight GBP in the pack.

**One-time vs ongoing.** This entire layer is **one-time, in-scope build work**: schema, NAP, map embed, aggregateRating, and unique location-page content are authored once and ship with the site. Ongoing client-managed off-page (reviews, GBP posts, link acquisition) is out of scope here. The one buildable off-page touch that is in scope is the **GBP-link target**: pointing the Google Business Profile at a purpose-built city/service landing page measurably moved pack rank within ~2 weeks in an independent test ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/does-the-url-you-link-to-in-google-my-business-impact-ranking-in-the-local-pack/)).

**Equity vs citation.** This pillar produces **entity-citation and structured-data signals, not link equity** — there are no dofollow backlinks here. `sameAs` is an entity-reconciliation/disambiguation aid that ties the business to its authoritative nodes (GBP, social, review, manufacturer find-a-pro); Google's own docs frame it as "additional information about your organization," never as a ranking multiplier ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization)). Schema overall is eligibility for rich results and appearance, explicitly **not** a ranking signal ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data)). Treat it as clarity/extraction infrastructure — a December-2024 study found **no correlation** between schema coverage and AI-citation rates ([searchengineland.com](https://searchengineland.com/schema-markup-ai-search-no-hype-472339)).

**The measured floor.** Two things are independently *measured*, not modeled: (1) hiding the address negatively correlates with pack rank — across 8,186 businesses in 200 cities, and on real clients restoring the address recovered "freefall" rankings ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/what-gets-you-ranking-for-near-me-2025/)); (2) pages with more *substantive* (non-stopword) words correlate with better local rank in that same study — content quality, not length ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/what-gets-you-ranking-for-near-me-2025/)). So a consistent shown NAP plus genuinely substantive per-city content is the defensible floor.

**The hard policy gate.** Unique per-city content is not a nice-to-have — it is a policy requirement. Google's first-party spam policy names "multiple domain names or pages targeted at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page" as doorway abuse, and AI-generated "many pages without adding value" as scaled-content abuse ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies)). The anti-doorway gate (real-job→page, delete-the-city-name test) is what keeps this build a ranking asset instead of a deindexing liability.

**Approximate one-time cost.** Schema/geo/`sameAs`, NAP, map embed, and aggregateRating are config-driven and effectively built into the site build (sub-$200 of marginal effort at template scale). The real cost is the *unique per-city content* required to clear the doorway gate — that scales with the number of real service cities (genuine job photos, local detail per page), and is the line item to budget against, not the markup.

**Impact vs effort.** High impact / low effort: schema + NAP + GBP-link-to-dedicated-landing (cheap, and the GBP-link target is measured). High impact / high effort: unique per-city content (the engine for organic dominance and the policy gate). Low impact regardless of effort: embedded maps lost direct ranking credit in June 2018 — they are now UX/trust/location-confirmation only ([gobluemedia.com](https://www.gobluemedia.com/blog/google-maps-seo-rankings/)) — and self-serving aggregateRating cannot earn star snippets ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet)).

**What NOT to oversell:** Never claim "our schema ranks you" — schema is eligibility/clarity, not a ranking signal ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data)); never promise embedded maps or aggregateRating as rank/star-snippet wins; never quote the unattributed "40% more likely" NAP stat or a "55% proximity" figure; and never sell the on-site layer as a pack-ranking lever — sell it as the organic engine plus the entity-verification layer, because the pack is proximity-capped and GBP-led.

loadBearing.claim: Google ranks local results on relevance, distance, and prominence; prominence explicitly counts links/articles/directories AND the business's position in organic web results, so on-site SEO feeds the pack via organic position.
loadBearing.stat: prominence = web links + reviews + organic web position (first-party)
loadBearing.snippet: Prominence is also based on information that Google has about a business from across the web, like links, articles, and directories. ... Your position in web results is also a factor, so search engine optimization (SEO) best practices apply.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the spine of the whole offer: Google's own words tie on-site/organic work to prominence, which is what justifies building a deep site for organic dominance. Anchors the 'organic engine' frame on a first-party source.

loadBearing.claim: Structured data is eligibility for rich results/appearance, NOT a ranking signal — so the on-site schema/sameAs layer is an entity-clarity and rich-result/AI-extraction lever, never a pack-ranking lever.
loadBearing.stat: n/a (qualitative first-party spec)
loadBearing.snippet: Adding structured data can enable search results that are more engaging to users and might encourage them to interact more with your website, which are called rich results.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The cardinal anti-oversell guardrail. Any reel implying schema 'ranks you' is FTC-exposed false confidence; this first-party doc is the proof to hold the honest frame.

loadBearing.claim: Independent test (8,186 businesses / 200 cities, 5 service categories): hiding the business address negatively correlates with local-pack rank, and restoring a hidden address recovered tanked client rankings — so a consistent SHOWN NAP is measured, load-bearing local proof.
loadBearing.stat: 8,186 businesses across 200 cities; address-hiding negatively correlated with pack rank
loadBearing.snippet: We found a negative correlation between hiding your address and ranking well in the local pack. ... Their rankings tanked. Like freefall tanked. ... [restored] their rankings jumped back up.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the strongest MEASURED, independent, large-N basis for the NAP/shown-address build element — replaces the unverifiable '40% more likely' vendor stat with a defensible floor claim.

loadBearing.claim: Independent test: changing a GBP's linked URL from homepage to a specific service page produced measurable local-pack ranking gains within ~2 weeks — the basis for the one-time, in-scope GBP-link-to-dedicated-landing build pattern.
loadBearing.stat: pack-rank improvement within ~2 weeks of changing GBP landing URL
loadBearing.snippet: The content on the specific URL you link to is important and impacts ranking in the local results.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The only buildable one-time off-page touch that is both in-scope and MEASURED to move the pack. Justifies shipping a purpose-built city/service landing as the GBP target.

loadBearing.claim: Google's first-party spam policy classifies city/region pages that funnel users to one page as doorway abuse, and AI-generated 'many pages without adding value' as scaled-content abuse — making genuinely unique per-city content a policy requirement, not just a quality preference.
loadBearing.stat: first-party policy: city/region doorway pages + AI scaled pages = spam violations
loadBearing.snippet: Having multiple domain names or pages targeted at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page ... Using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the BLOCKING gate that defines what the local-proof layer must be. Anchors the anti-doorway discipline on first-party policy and protects the offer from a deindexing-risk objection.

loadBearing.claim: Independent Dec-2024 study found NO correlation between schema-markup coverage and AI-citation rates — schema is extraction infrastructure, not an AI-citation or ranking driver; this debunks vendor '28-40% more citations' claims.
loadBearing.stat: no correlation between schema coverage and AI-citation rate
loadBearing.snippet: LLMs prioritize relevance, topical authority, and semantic clarity over whether content has structured markup ... infrastructure, not a magic bullet.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Directly bounds the AI-citation upside of the schema/sameAs layer. Keeps the offer from inheriting the vendor over-claim that schema 'drives AI citations' — promise clarity/eligibility, never the citation ceiling.

whatNotToOversell: Never claim 'our schema ranks you' — structured data is eligibility for rich results and entity-understanding, explicitly NOT a ranking signal (developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data).
Never sell sameAs/geo/areaServed as a rank multiplier — it is entity disambiguation/clarity; benefit is AI-extraction accuracy and trust, directional not ranking.
Never claim schema drives AI citations — a Dec-2024 independent study found no correlation between schema coverage and AI-citation rates (searchengineland.com/schema-markup-ai-search-no-hype-472339).
Never present the embedded map as a ranking lever — Google ended direct map-embed ranking credit in June 2018; it is UX/trust/location-confirmation only (gobluemedia.com).

Never imply self-serving aggregateRating earns star snippets — self-reviewed LocalBusiness/Organization pages are ineligible for the star rich result (developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet).
Never quote 'consistent NAP = 40% more likely to appear in the pack' — unattributed on BrightLocal's own page; promise only the measured floor (shown address helps; hiding it measurably hurts).
Never quote a 'proximity 55%' single-factor figure — Sterling Sky's 8,186-business study publishes no single-factor percentage and says there is no magic factor.

Never sell the on-site layer as a PACK-ranking lever — on-page is ~15% of pack vs ~33% of organic; the pack is proximity-capped and GBP-led. Sell organic dominance + entity verification, not pack lift.
Never cite the agency-blog 'dedicated city page = +25 positions in weeks' result — single-client, unverified; use the measured GBP-link-URL test instead.
Never promise dofollow link equity from this pillar — it produces entity-citation and structured-data signals, not backlinks; no PBN/link-scheme/gray-hat is in scope, ever.
gaps: No primary/independent A/B isolating sameAs-only impact on either pack or organic rank (mechanism is documented; magnitude is not measured) — keep sameAs framed as directional entity-clarity.

No measured effect size for KM's specific GBP->dedicated-landing pattern in ROOFING (Sterling Sky's positive test was a NYC personal-injury practitioner listing); roofing is single-location-skewed where homepage often still wins — claim is directional for single-location roofers.

Could not load the Whitespark report body directly (JS-rendered); pack/organic weights are corroborated via a secondary that quotes the survey verbatim, not the source HTML — still a MODELED expert survey regardless.
No primary source confirming the ~14-21 day sameAs reconciliation lag (single secondary blog) — treat timeline as illustrative, not a promise.

Did not separately verify areaServed/LocalBusiness geo as a ranking input (Google docs only frame geo for location display, not ranking) — areaServed remains a relevance/clarity + content lever, not a measured rank factor.

No PRIMARY/independent (non-agency-blog) controlled study isolating roofing-vertical or NC/Triangle-specific on-site local-proof impact was found; the strongest independent local data (Sterling Sky near-me 2025) covers plumber/HVAC/locksmith/garage/lawn, NOT roofing — roofing-vertical specificity remains a directional extrapolation, not measured.

The vendor 'consistent entity info increases LLM citation probability 28-40%' figure (WebFX / averi.ai / digital-bloom) has NO traceable primary methodology; it is vendor-incentive and is actively contradicted by the Dec-2024 no-correlation finding. Needs a named, reproducible study before any version is usable in a reel — currently exclude.

Quantified, independent measurement of how much an on-site sameAs/Organization entity-lock actually moves AI-Overview/LLM citation share for a local home-services business is absent; current evidence supports CLARITY/extraction only, not a measurable citation lift. Treat the entity-lock benefit as directional.

No primary source was found quantifying the incremental organic lift of embedded-map / driving-directions vs. a page without them (Round 1 already established these lost direct SEO credit in 2018); remains a UX/trust claim only.

Exact correlation coefficients / effect sizes from the Sterling Sky study are not published in the public article (it reports direction, not magnitude) — so 'substantive words help' is directionally measured but not a quantified promise.

counter.point: Google's first-party docs never call structured data (sameAs/geo/areaServed) a ranking factor — only an eligibility/appearance + entity-understanding aid. Any pitch that implies 'our schema ranks you' is FTC-exposed false confidence.
counter.soWhat: Frame the on-site schema layer as entity-clarity + rich-result/AI-citation eligibility + trust, and route the actual ranking story to ORGANIC position (links/on-page) which prominence explicitly counts.

counter.point: On-site alone does not move the PACK: surveys put on-page at ~15% and citations ~6% of pack weight, with GBP (32%) + reviews (20%) + proximity dominating. The pack is proximity-capped and largely off-page-driven.
counter.soWhat: Sell organic regional dominance (on-page 33% + links 24%) as the engine; treat the pack as the proximity-capped byproduct. Don't center the pack or over-claim on-site pack lift.

counter.point: Embedded maps lost direct ranking credit in 2018; self-serving aggregateRating can't earn star snippets. Two of the flashiest 'local proof' on-site elements are trust/UX-only, not ranking or rich-result wins.
counter.soWhat: Keep them for conversion/trust/location-confirmation, and be explicit they're not rank levers — protects against the polished-false-confidence cardinal sin.

counter.point: The headline NAP stat '40% more likely' and the 'proximity 55%' figure both fail to trace to a primary table (BrightLocal page is self-unattributed; Sterling Sky's 8,186-study explicitly publishes NO single-factor percentage and says there's no magic factor).
counter.soWhat: Promise the FLOOR (consistent shown NAP supports prominence/proximity; address-hiding measurably hurts) and drop the unverifiable point-percentages from any reel/pitch.

counter.point: A December-2024 independent study (cited by Search Engine Land) found NO correlation between schema-markup coverage and AI-citation rates — sites with comprehensive structured data did not consistently outperform those with minimal markup; LLMs 'prioritize relevance, topical authority, and semantic clarity over whether content has structured markup.' Schema is 'infrastructure, not a magic bullet.'
counter.soWhat: Hard guardrail on the on-site schema/sameAs layer: KM can position schema as entity-CLARITY + extraction-accuracy infrastructure, but must NOT claim it drives AI citations or rankings. Directly debunks the vendor 'consistent entity data increases LLM citation 28-40%' figure (vendor-incentive, unattributed). Promise the floor (clarity/eligibility), never the ceiling (citations).

counter.point: A skeptic's strongest frame: in the PACK specifically, GBP signals (~32%) plus proximity dominate, while on-page is a minority (~15-19%). A strong website with no/weak GBP 'will almost never appear in the Local 3-Pack.' Multiple independent Sterling Sky controlled tests found ZERO pack-ranking movement from GBP posts (9-week, 441-keyword study) and from geotagged photos (27 locations).
counter.soWhat: Reinforces the SPINE, doesn't break it: the on-site layer's biggest payoff is ORGANIC regional dominance (on-page is the #1 organic lever) and entity clarity/AI — NOT pack rank, which is proximity-capped and GBP-led. Honestly: the website corroborates/verifies GBP rather than out-weighting it in the pack. Don't sell on-site work as a pack-ranking lever; sell it as the organic engine + the trust/verification layer.

counter.point: The 'create a dedicated page per city and rankings jump 25 positions in weeks' case-study results circulating for 2025 are AGENCY-BLOG, single-client, n=1 anecdotes (Revved, MapRanks, lseo) — not controlled studies. They are directional only and survivorship-biased (failed location-page rollouts that got deindexed don't get blogged).
counter.soWhat: Do NOT promise a position-count lift from launching city pages. The defensible claim is the FLOOR: unique per-city pages are eligible to rank organically and avoid the deindex risk thin pages carry; the CEILING (big jumps) is possible but unproven at population level. Cite the measured Sterling Sky 'substantive words' correlation for the floor, not the n=1 jumps.

allClaims.claim: Google's own LocalBusiness structured-data docs recommend the geo property (lat/long) and require precision of at least 5 decimal places, establishing the business's physical location for Search/Maps features — this is the buildable, config-driven geo-coordinate proof on-site.
allClaims.stat: geo precision >= 5 decimal places (recommended property)
allClaims.snippet: Geographic coordinates of the business. ... The precision must be at least 5 decimal places.

allClaims.claim: Google's Organization structured-data docs define sameAs as URLs to other authoritative pages about the org (social/review profiles) and recommend including multiple — Google uses these for entity disambiguation/reconciliation, NOT as a stated ranking multiplier. sameAs locks entity CLARITY, it does not 'boost' rank.
allClaims.stat: n/a (qualitative spec)
allClaims.snippet: The URL of a page on another website with additional information about your organization, if applicable. For example, a URL to your organization's profile page on a social media or review site. ... you can specify multiple sameAs URLs

allClaims.claim: Google explicitly frames structured data as eligibility for RICH RESULTS / appearance, NOT a ranking signal — so the on-site schema/sameAs layer is honestly an entity-clarity + rich-result + AI-citation lever, not a pack-ranking lever. This is the core anti-oversell honesty guardrail for the offer.
allClaims.stat: n/a
allClaims.snippet: Adding structured data can enable search results that are more engaging to users and might encourage them to interact more with your website, which are called rich results.

allClaims.claim: Google ranks local results on relevance, distance, and PROMINENCE; prominence is explicitly based on info from across the web — how many websites link to the business, reviews, plus a business's position in (organic) web results. This is the spine: on-site work feeds Prominence via the entity's organic web position, and links move organic far more than the pack.
allClaims.stat: prominence factors: web links + reviews + organic web position
allClaims.snippet: Prominence is also based on information that Google has about a business from across the web, like links, articles, and directories. ... Your position in web results is also a factor, so search engine optimization (SEO) best practices apply.

allClaims.claim: Self-serving reviews (a business marking up reviews about ITSELF on its own LocalBusiness/Organization pages — incl. embedded GBP/Facebook widgets) are INELIGIBLE for the star review rich result. KM's on-site aggregateRating is therefore a content/AI/trust signal, never a star-snippet play; star rich results require third-party/Product schema. Hard FTC-adjacent honesty rule.
allClaims.stat: n/a (policy, since 2019)
allClaims.snippet: If the entity that's being reviewed controls the reviews about itself, their pages that use LocalBusiness or any other type of Organization structured data are ineligible for star review feature.

allClaims.claim: INDEPENDENT TEST: Sterling Sky analyzed 8,186 businesses across 200 cities (plumber/HVAC/locksmith/garage-door/lawn) and found a NEGATIVE correlation between HIDING the address and ranking in the local pack; on real clients, hiding the address tanked rankings and restoring it recovered them. Validates that a consistent, SHOWN NAP + real service-area address is load-bearing local proof — and that proximity/address gating is real but they did NOT publish a '55%' figure.
allClaims.stat: 8,186 businesses / 200 cities; address-hiding negatively correlated with pack rank
allClaims.snippet: We found a negative correlation between hiding your address and ranking well in the local pack. ... Their rankings tanked. Like freefall tanked. ... [restored] their rankings jumped back up.

allClaims.claim: INDEPENDENT TEST: Sterling Sky changed a GBP's linked URL from the homepage to a specific service page and saw measurable local-pack ranking gains within ~2 weeks — 'the content on the specific URL you link to is important and impacts ranking in the local results.' This is the measured basis for the GBP-link -> dedicated-landing pattern KM builds (config-driven per-city/service landing target).
allClaims.stat: ranking improvement within ~2 weeks of changing GBP landing URL
allClaims.snippet: The content on the specific URL you link to is important and impacts ranking in the local results.

allClaims.claim: ANTI-CANNIBALIZATION NUANCE (post Feb-2025 Diversity Update): Sterling Sky now warns that pointing a GBP at a page ALREADY ranking organically can HURT organic; target a relevant page that isn't already ranking. So the buildable dedicated GBP-landing must be a purpose-built city/service page, not the homepage or top organic page — exactly the config-driven landing KM ships.
allClaims.stat: n/a (qualitative, Feb 2025 update)
allClaims.snippet: Google's Diversity Update changed this ... linking GBP listings to high-ranking organic pages can now hurt organic rankings, so they recommend targeting relevant pages that aren't already ranking organically.

allClaims.claim: Whitespark 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors (47 experts, 187 factors — EXPERT-SURVEY = MODELED): PACK = GBP 32% / reviews 20% / on-page 15% / behavioral 9% / links 8% / citations 6%; ORGANIC = on-page 33% / links 24% / behavioral 10% / GBP 7% / citations 7% / reviews 6%. On-site local-proof (on-page + citations) is a minority of the PACK but on-page is the #1 ORGANIC lever — reinforcing the organic-dominance spine.
allClaims.stat: Pack on-page 15% + citations 6%; Organic on-page 33% + links 24%
allClaims.snippet: Google Business Profile (GBP) Signals - 32%, Review Signals - 20%, On-Page Signals - 15% ... [Organic] On-Page Signals - 33%, Link Signals - 24% ... 47 local search experts reviewing 187 factors

allClaims.claim: EMBEDDED MAP HONESTY: Google removed the direct local-SEO 'credit' for embedding a map on a landing page in June 2018 (abuse-driven). An embedded map is now a UX/trust + location-confirmation signal that ties the page to the GBP/physical location — NOT a ranking lever. KM ships embedded map + driving directions for conversion/trust, not as a rank claim.
allClaims.stat: direct map-embed ranking credit ended June 2018
allClaims.snippet: Until 2018 ... embedding Google Maps on landing pages with your address lent more credence to local SEO ... Google made it clear they didn't want this practice anymore and put an end to it in June 2018 ... not giving you any credits for that map feature anymore.

allClaims.claim: Citation/NAP signals are a MINORITY direct weight (~6-9% of pack) per the surveys — consistent NAP supports prominence and proximity rather than being a standalone ranking category. The widely-quoted 'consistent NAP = 40% more likely to appear in the pack' stat is UNATTRIBUTED in BrightLocal's own page; treat as DIRECTIONAL, do NOT promise it.
allClaims.stat: citations ~6% (pack) / ~9% blended; '40%' stat unattributed
allClaims.snippet: Businesses with consistent NAP data across major citation sources are 40% more likely to appear in the local pack. [no attribution provided on page] ... Accurate NAP information helps establish prominence and proximity signals.

allClaims.claim: sameAs feeds entity reconciliation into Google's Knowledge Graph (500B+ facts on 5B+ entities), merging multi-source info into one entity record — strongest when sameAs points to AUTHORITATIVE nodes (Wikidata/Wikipedia, then GBP/social/review profiles). For a roofer with no Wikipedia node, sameAs -> GBP + manufacturer find-a-pro + verified directories is the realistic, buildable entity-lock; benefit is CLARITY/AI-citation, directional not a rank multiplier.
allClaims.stat: Knowledge Graph 500B+ facts / 5B+ entities; ~14-21 day reconciliation lag (modeled)
allClaims.snippet: sameAs ... Google and AI systems use these links to merge information from multiple sources into a single entity record ... estimated 14- to 21-day algorithmic lag between deploying valid sameAs triples and full node reconciliation.

allClaims.claim: Sterling Sky's 8,186-business / 200-city near-me study found a MEASURED positive correlation between the amount of substantive (non-stopword) words on a page and better local-pack rankings — 'more meaningful words' correlate, raw word count does not. This is the strongest independent, measured basis that on-site CONTENT QUALITY (not length) is a real local-proof lever KM can build.
allClaims.stat: 8,186 businesses across 200 cities (100 large / 50 mid / 50 small), 5 service categories (plumber, HVAC, locksmith, garage door, lawn care); slight positive correlation: substantive words -> better local ranking
allClaims.snippet: there's a slight correlation between having more substantive words on your page and better local rankings ... More words does not equal better rankings. More meaningful words? That's a different story.

allClaims.claim: Google's PRIMARY spam-policy page defines doorway abuse to explicitly include 'multiple domain names or pages targeted at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page,' and defines scaled-content abuse to include 'using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value.' This is the authoritative, first-party basis for KM's anti-doorway BLOCKING gate (real-job -> page; delete-the-city-name test) — the buildable local-proof layer must be genuinely unique per city or it is a policy violation, not just weak.
allClaims.stat: First-party Google policy: city/region doorway pages + AI-generated scaled pages 'without adding value' are spam-policy violations
allClaims.snippet: Having multiple domain names or pages targeted at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page ... Using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value

allClaims.claim: INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of the anti-doorway gate: Google's Aug-Oct 2022 helpful-content + spam updates DEINDEXED duplicate-content location pages on service-area-business sites — pages that existed 'for the sole purpose of ranking [city] + [service] multiplied by the number of cities.' Higher-authority sites and pages with genuinely UNIQUE per-city content were NOT deindexed. Confirms KM's per-city uniqueness requirement is load-bearing risk mitigation, and that thin location pages can REMOVE you from the index entirely (downside is deindex, not just no-lift).
